$comment: The root of trust for MSYS2 package signatures (#236, W1-R-B §2.2).
WHAT THIS DECIDES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
The committed lock is the INTEGRITY decision: an archive is admitted only if
its SHA-256 equals the reviewed value, and no signature can change that.
This trust root is the ATTRIBUTION decision: it proves the exact bytes the
lock names were signed by an MSYS2 packager we accept, rather than merely
matching a digest somebody recorded from the same compromised mirror.
Both must hold. Neither substitutes for the other.
WHY IT IS THIS SMALL.
Every one of the 246 locked archives is signed by exactly one key. Pinning
the whole 12-key MSYS2 keyring would accept eleven signers that sign nothing
here, including four that msys2-revoked revokes. The allowlist is therefore
the measured signer set, not the published keyring: a package signed by a
different MSYS2 packager fails closed and has to be re-reviewed.
HOW THE MATERIAL WAS DERIVED.
From the msys2-keyring package named below -- which is itself a member of
the lock, so its bytes are digest-pinned by the same mechanism as every
other archive -- by extracting usr/share/pacman/keyrings/msys2.gpg,
importing it into an empty GnuPG home, and exporting the accepted
fingerprint alone:
tar --zstd -xOf <keyring>.pkg.tar.zst usr/share/pacman/keyrings/msys2.gpg \
| gpg --homedir <empty> --import
gpg --homedir <empty> --export --armor \
--export-options export-minimal <fingerprint> > msys2-signing-keys.asc
keyFileSha256 is checked on every use, so the committed bytes are the
decision rather than whatever a re-derivation happens to produce.
